OK-2026-SB259.aiSummary: Approved by the governor, the measure changes how groundwater use is permitted, metered, reported, and checked in Oklahoma. It requires more reporting for permit holders, adds rules for some animal feeding operations, and lets the Water Resources Board investigate complaints and set fines or other penalties for waste. It also expands meter or measuring system use for wells that need a permit, and limits permits for some data center cooling systems unless they use lower-water cooling methods.

OK-2026-SB1632.aiSummary: The bill would have the State Department of Education approve career-readiness tests and related credentials for public school students. Starting in the 2026-2027 school year, these tests would be available to students in grades 10 through 12, and districts could give them at no cost to students who choose to take them. It also lets state higher education officials write rules so colleges may give credit for these test results and credentials; the bill was approved by the governor and takes effect July 1, 2026.

OK-2026-SB1338.aiSummary: The bill would create a new state fund for the Education Department to award competitive grants for education projects that aim to improve student learning in Oklahoma. The State Board of Education would review and score grant applications, and the names of applicants would be removed before review. The fund could take in state money, gifts, grants, donations, and bequests, and the act would take effect November 1, 2026.

OK-2026-HB3521.aiSummary: The act creates a new state law for money transmission services and replaces the old rules. It requires most money transmission businesses to get a license, and it sets rules for applications, renewals, records, funds, and state oversight. It also creates felony penalties for some false records or for doing licensed money transmission work without a license.
